from manim import *
import numpy as np
import random

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup
        title = "The Unstructured Search Problem"
        lines = [
            "Imagine searching an unsorted database of one thousand items.",
            "Classically, we must check every item one by one.",
            "This linear search takes up to one thousand attempts."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors for lecture steps
        color_step1 = "#87CEEB" # Sky Blue
        color_step2 = "#FFFFE0" # Light Yellow
        color_step3 = "#FFB6C1" # Light Pink

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_step1))
        
        # Create 1,000 small dark green circles (#556B2F)
        # 40 columns x 25 rows = 1,000
        circles = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=0.04, color="#556B2F", fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0.5) 
            for _ in range(1000)
        ])
        circles.arrange_in_grid(rows=25, cols=40, buff=0.06)
        
        # Place the grid in area A1 to F6
        self.place_in_area(circles, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(circles, run_time=2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_step2))
        
        # One random circle flashes Gold (#FFD700)
        target_index = 842 # Randomly chosen far into the list
        target_circle = circles[target_index]
        
        self.play(target_circle.animate.set_color("#FFD700").scale(1.5), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(target_circle.animate.scale(1/1.5), run_time=0.5)
        
        # A white highlight box (#FFFFFF) scans the grid circles one-by-one
        scanner = Square(side_length=0.15, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=2)
        scanner.move_to(circles[0].get_center())
        
        self.add(scanner)
        
        # Animate scanner for the first few items to show "one by one"
        # Then skip ahead to demonstrate complexity
        scan_indices = list(range(0, 15)) + list(range(15, 80, 5)) 
        
        for idx in scan_indices:
            self.play(scanner.animate.move_to(circles[idx].get_center()), run_time=0.05)
            
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_step3))
        
        # Fast scan towards the end to emphasize "one thousand attempts"
        fast_indices = [200, 400, 600, 800, target_index]
        for idx in fast_indices:
            self.play(scanner.animate.move_to(circles[idx].get_center()), run_time=0.2)
        
        self.play(Indicate(target_circle, color="#FFD700"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        lecture_lines = [
            'Quantum computers represent all items as a state vector.', 
            'We create a uniform superposition of every possible state.', 
            'Initially, every item has the same probability amplitude.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Superposition & State Vectors", lecture_lines)

        # Pre-create bars for efficiency
        # Using 500 bars to maintain high visual density (Mist effect) while ensuring render speed
        # Color: Light Blue (#ADD8E6)
        num_bars = 500 
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Line(ORIGIN, UP * 0.05, stroke_width=1.5, color="#ADD8E6") 
            for _ in range(num_bars)
        ])
        bars.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.006)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight current line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=0.5)
        
        # A bar chart appears with thin, zero-height bars along the x-axis.
        # We place them at the bottom of the right-side grid area (Row E)
        self.place_in_area(bars, "E1", "E6")
        self.play(FadeIn(bars))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition highlight
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # All bars simultaneously rise to a height representing 1/sqrt(1000)
        # Visually, we grow them to occupy a significant portion of the grid
        self.play(
            bars.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(3.0, about_edge=DOWN),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition highlight
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # A text label 'Uniform Superposition' appears in White (#FFFFFF) above the bars.
        # Positioned in grid row B (above the bars in E)
        label = Text("Uniform Superposition", font_size=28, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(label, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(label))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        YELLOW_C = "#FFFF00"
        GOLD_C = "#FFD700"
        CYAN_C = "#00FFFF"
        
        lines = [
            'The Oracle is a function that identifies our target.',
            'It recognizes the correct item without revealing its location.',
            "Mathematically, the Oracle flips the target's phase.",
            "The target's amplitude points downward on our chart.",
            'Its probability remains unchanged at this specific stage.'
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)", lines)
        
        # --- Persistent Components ---
        # Bar Chart Setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 9, 1],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E6")
        
        # Bars initialization (8 bars)
        base_height = 1.2
        bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(1, 9):
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.3,
                height=base_height,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                color=BLUE_D,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i, base_height/2))
            bars.add(bar)
            
        target_index = 3 # Index 0-7, corresponds to bar at x=4
        target_bar = bars[target_index]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW_C))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(bars))
        self.play(target_bar.animate.set_color(YELLOW_C))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW_C))
        self.play(Indicate(target_bar, color=YELLOW_C))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CYAN_C))
        
        # Replacement for MathTex due to environment limitations (missing latex)
        formula = Text("|w⟩ → -|w⟩", color=CYAN_C, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "A4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(
            target_bar.animate.rotate(PI, axis=RIGHT, about_point=axes.c2p(4, 0)),
            Write(formula)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GOLD_C))
        
        # Amplitude Label using Text instead of MathTex
        label = Text("-1/√N", color=GOLD_C, font_size=24)
        label.next_to(target_bar, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(GOLD_C))
        
        # Probability formula using Text instead of MathTex
        prob_formula = Text("|-a|² = |a|²", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(prob_formula, "A2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(prob_formula))
        self.play(Indicate(target_bar))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup standard layout
        lecture_lines = [
            'Next, we apply the Grover diffusion operator.',
            'We calculate the average amplitude of all states.',
            'Every amplitude is reflected across this average line.',
            "The target's amplitude grows significantly taller than others.",
            'The non-target amplitudes shrink slightly in comparison.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Reflection about the Mean)", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_TARGET = "#FFD700"  # Gold
        COLOR_NON_TARGET = "#50C878"  # Emerald Green
        COLOR_MEAN = "#FFFFFF"  # White
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a set of bars representing amplitudes after the Oracle step
        # Target is at index 2, flipped negative
        initial_heights = [1.2, 1.2, -1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 1.2]
        bar_colors = [COLOR_NON_TARGET] * 8
        bar_colors[2] = COLOR_TARGET
        
        # We'll use a local coordinate system for the bars within the grid area
        chart_area_tl = "B2"
        chart_area_br = "E6"
        
        bars = VGroup()
        bar_width = 0.4
        spacing = 0.1
        
        for i, h in enumerate(initial_heights):
            # Create a rectangle with height h. 
            # Height in Manim units corresponds to the amplitude value.
            rect = Rectangle(
                width=bar_width, 
                height=abs(h), 
                fill_opacity=0.8, 
                fill_color=bar_colors[i],
                stroke_width=1
            )
            # Align the base of the bar to the "zero" line
            if h >= 0:
                rect.align_to(ORIGIN, DOWN)
            else:
                rect.align_to(ORIGIN, UP)
            
            rect.shift(RIGHT * i * (bar_width + spacing))
            bars.add(rect)
            
        # Add a zero baseline
        baseline = Line(
            bars.get_left() + LEFT * 0.2, 
            bars.get_right() + RIGHT * 0.2, 
            color=GRAY, 
            stroke_width=2
        )
        chart = VGroup(baseline, bars)
        self.place_in_area(chart, chart_area_tl, chart_area_br, scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(chart))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Calculate mean: (7 * 1.2 - 1.2) / 8 = 7.2 / 8 = 0.9
        mean_val = sum(initial_heights) / len(initial_heights)
        
        # Find the vertical position of the mean value relative to baseline
        # Since bars are scaled and moved, we use the baseline as Y=0 reference
        mean_y = baseline.get_y() + mean_val * (bars[0].height / abs(initial_heights[0]))
        
        mean_line = DashedLine(
            start=[baseline.get_left()[0], mean_y, 0],
            end=[baseline.get_right()[0], mean_y, 0],
            color=COLOR_MEAN,
            stroke_width=3
        )
        mean_label = Text("Mean", font_size=16, color=COLOR_MEAN).next_to(mean_line, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(mean_line), Write(mean_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Reflection logic: H_new = 2 * Mean - H_old
        # Mean = 0.9
        # Non-target: 2 * 0.9 - 1.2 = 1.8 - 1.2 = 0.6
        # Target: 2 * 0.9 - (-1.2) = 1.8 + 1.2 = 3.0
        
        new_heights = [2 * mean_val - h for h in initial_heights]
        
        # Transform bars
        # Note: We must be careful about scaling rectangles.
        # We'll create new rectangles and transform them.
        
        new_bars = VGroup()
        for i, (h_old, h_new) in enumerate(zip(initial_heights, new_heights)):
            new_rect = Rectangle(
                width=bar_width, 
                height=abs(h_new), 
                fill_opacity=0.8, 
                fill_color=bar_colors[i],
                stroke_width=1
            )
            # Match horizontal position
            new_rect.move_to(bars[i].get_center())
            new_rect.set_x(bars[i].get_x())
            
            # Align to baseline
            if h_new >= 0:
                new_rect.align_to(baseline, DOWN)
            else:
                new_rect.align_to(baseline, UP)
            
            new_bars.add(new_rect)
            
        # First animation: move tips to mean (visual representation of reflection)
        # We can't easily animate the rectangle height around the mean without custom updaters,
        # so we'll use a direct ReplacementTransform for clarity of the "reflection" result.
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(bars, new_bars),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Focus on target bar (index 2)
        target_bar = new_bars[2]
        surround_rect = SurroundingRectangle(target_bar, color=COLOR_TARGET, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(surround_rect))
        self.play(Indicate(target_bar, color=COLOR_TARGET))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Show comparison with non-target bars
        non_targets = VGroup(*[new_bars[i] for i in range(len(new_bars)) if i != 2])
        self.play(FadeOut(surround_rect))
        self.play(non_targets.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.4))
        self.play(Indicate(non_targets))
        
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Clean up for next section (optional, usually scene ends here)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define Section 5 content
        title = "Geometric Interpretation: Grover's Rotation"
        lines = [
            "- Subspace spanned by |w> and |s'>",
            "- |s'> is the average of non-targets",
            "- Initial state |s> has angle theta",
            "- Oracle (Uw): Reflects across |s'>",
            "- Diffusion (Us): Reflects across |s>",
            "- Combined: Rotate by 2*theta per step"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Right-side Visualization: Geometric Vectors
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY}
        )
        self.place_at_grid(axes, "C3")

        # Labels - Switched from MathTex to Text to avoid dependency on missing 'latex' executable
        label_w = Text("|w>", color=RED, font_size=24).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 1.3) + LEFT * 0.4)
        label_s_prime = Text("|s'>", color=BLUE, font_size=24).move_to(axes.c2p(1.3, 0) + DOWN * 0.4)

        # Initial state vector |s>
        theta = 15 * DEGREES
        vec_s = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(np.cos(theta), np.sin(theta)), buff=0, color=YELLOW)
        label_s = Text("|s>", color=YELLOW, font_size=24).next_to(vec_s.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # Animation Sequence
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(label_w), Write(label_s_prime))
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_s), Write(label_s))
        self.wait(1)

        # Oracle reflection (Reflect across s' axis - visual approximation)
        vec_s_ref = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(np.cos(-theta), np.sin(-theta)), buff=0, color=PURPLE)
        label_uw = Text("Uw|s>", color=PURPLE, font_size=20).next_to(vec_s_ref.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            TransformFromCopy(vec_s, vec_s_ref),
            FadeIn(label_uw)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Diffusion reflection (Resulting rotation)
        vec_final = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(np.cos(3*theta), np.sin(3*theta)), buff=0, color=GREEN)
        label_g = Text("G|s>", color=GREEN, font_size=24).next_to(vec_final.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(vec_s_ref, vec_final),
            FadeOut(label_uw),
            FadeIn(label_g)
        )
        self.wait(2)
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'Grover’s algorithm provides a massive quadratic speedup.',
            'A million items require only one thousand quantum steps.',
            'This efficiency transforms cryptography and complex logistics optimization.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Quantum Advantage", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Description: The text 'Classical: O(N)' in Red (#FF0000) appears on the left.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(RED))
        
        classical_label = Text("Classical: ", font_size=32, color="#FF0000")
        classical_math = Text("O(N)", font_size=32, color="#FF0000")
        classical_group = VGroup(classical_label, classical_math).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(classical_group, 'B1', 'B3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(classical_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Description: The text 'Quantum: O(√N)' in Green (#00FF00) appears on the right.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN)
        )
        
        quantum_label = Text("Quantum: ", font_size=32, color="#00FF00")
        quantum_math = Text("O(√N)", font_size=32, color="#00FF00")
        quantum_group = VGroup(quantum_label, quantum_math).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(quantum_group, 'B4', 'B6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(quantum_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Description: A direct comparison '1,000,000 vs 1,000' flashes to emphasize the speedup.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        comp_left = Text("1,000,000", font_size=36, color="#FF0000")
        comp_vs = Text("vs", font_size=28, color=WHITE)
        comp_right = Text("1,000", font_size=36, color="#00FF00")
        
        self.place_at_grid(comp_left, 'D2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_in_area(comp_vs, 'D3', 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(comp_right, 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        comparison_group = VGroup(comp_left, comp_vs, comp_right)
        
        # Flashing effect as requested
        for _ in range(3):
            self.play(FadeIn(comparison_group), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(FadeOut(comparison_group), run_time=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(comparison_group))
        self.wait(3)

        # Wrap up: Reset highlights
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Grover's Algorithm: The Quantum Search for a Needle in a Haystack
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in computer science or physics

sections.title: The Unstructured Search Problem
sections.content: Introduce the challenge of finding a specific item in an unsorted database. Explain the limitation of classical search (O(N)) where you must check every item one by one.
sections.example: Imagine a school of 1,000 identical-looking green fish hidden in a coral reef. Only one of them, 'Goldie', is actually made of gold. A classical diver must check each fish individually, taking up to 1,000 attempts.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Superposition & State Vectors
sections.content: Explain that in quantum computing, we don't look at fish one by one. We represent all possible fish as a 'state vector'. Using N qubits, we create a 'uniform superposition' where every fish has the same initial probability amplitude.
sections.example: Visually represent this as a bar chart with 1,000 bars of equal height (1/√N). This represents the 'Quantum Mist' where every fish exists simultaneously.

sections.title: Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)
sections.content: The Oracle is a 'black box' function that recognizes the target. Mathematically, it flips the sign (phase) of the target item's amplitude from positive to negative, while leaving others unchanged.
sections.example: In our bar chart, the bar corresponding to 'Goldie' suddenly flips upside down, pointing below the horizontal axis. It’s marked, but its probability (the square of the amplitude) remains the same as the others.

sections.title: Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Reflection about the Mean)
sections.content: This is the 'Grover iteration' magic. We calculate the average height of all bars. Then, we reflect every bar across this average line. Because Goldie's bar was far below the average, the reflection pushes it significantly above the others.
sections.example: Visualize a dotted 'mean line' just below the top of the green bars. After the reflection, Goldie’s bar shoots up like a skyscraper, while the 999 green fish bars shrink slightly.

sections.title: Iteration and Measurement
sections.content: Explain that repeating the Oracle and Diffusion steps increases the target's probability. Crucially, we only need to repeat this roughly √N times (approx. 32 times for 1,000 fish) before measuring the state.
sections.example: An animation showing the 'Goldie' bar growing taller with each pulse of light. After 32 pulses, we 'net' the fish; because Goldie's bar is at 99.9% height, we almost certainly catch the golden fish on the first try.

sections.title: The Quantum Advantage
sections.content: Summarize the quadratic speedup. Compare O(N) vs O(√N). Discuss real-world implications like breaking symmetric encryption or optimizing complex logistics.
sections.example: If the database had 1,000,000 items, a classical computer takes 1,000,000 steps, but Grover’s algorithm needs only 1,000 steps—a massive leap in efficiency.
